sections.title: One ending, any verb
sections.content: You already learned that szeretnék ("I would like") is szeret plus the conditional ending -nék, not the ordinary present-tense -k. That ending isn't unique to szeret — it attaches to any verb's stem to say "I would...": várnék ("I would wait"), tanulnék ("I would learn"), dolgoznék ("I would work"). Same idea, same ending, any verb.
-nék never changes for vowel harmony — it's always -nék, whether the verb is back-harmony (várnék) or front-harmony (kérnék). Only whether a linking vowel comes before it depends on the stem.
